title: Research
text:
Previous Research
Before joining the Department of Mathematics at Rice University, I worked with Matthias Heinkenschloss in Rice’s Department of Computational Applied Mathematics and Operations Research. My research focused on parameter identifiability and local solution manifolds of nonlinear least squares problems.


Undergraduate and Earlier Projects

Blocking Numbers of Convex Bodies
Bachelor’s thesis at the Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology, supervised by Alexander Polyanskii.
Max-sum Matchings of Points
Undergraduate research project at MIPT, supervised by Alexander Polyanskii.
The project focused on the conjecture posed by Andy Fingerhut in 1995, concerning the intersection of ellipses induced by a maximal-sum matching of an even set of points in the plane. The conjecture was later resolved by P. Barabanshchikova and A. Polyanskii in Intersecting Ellipses Induced by a Max-Sum Matching.
Rigidity of Laman Graphs and the Bellows Conjecture
Research practicum thesis at MIPT, supervised by Alexander Polyanskii.
I studied applications of the theory of places, an algebraic tool used in the proof of the Bellows Conjecture, and applied it to obtain a new proof of the rigidity of Laman graphs.

My undergraduate thesis, supervised by Alexander Polyanskii, studied blocking and covering numbers of convex bodies.

title: Fedor V. Gerasimov
text:
Title:
Exploring Local Solution Manifolds of Nonlinear Least Squares Problems


Abstract:
This poster presents a characterization of the local solution manifold of rank-deficient nonlinear least squares problems, in which the Jacobian has constant rank in a neighborhood of a solution. We also present an initial approach to computationally exploring the local solution manifold. Parameter estimation problems in some computational neuron models lead to nonlinear least squares problems of this type. Identifying local solution manifolds provides important information to neuroscientists. The proposed characterization of the local solution manifold is based on the constant rank theorem and on a subset selection algorithm. A version of the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm using subset selection is used to compute local solutions. The approach is used to compute local solution manifolds in an HCN channel model.

title: Maximum-sum matchings of points
text:
This was an undergraduate research project at the Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology, supervised by Alexander Polyanskii.
Given an even number of points in the Euclidean plane, a maximum-sum matching is a perfect matching that maximizes the sum of the Euclidean lengths of its matched pairs.
A motivating question, posed by Andy Fingerhut in 1995, asks whether certain ellipses induced by the edges of a maximum-sum matching must have a common intersection point. More precisely, for each matched pair, consider the ellipse with foci at the two endpoints and eccentricity \(\sqrt{3}/2\). Barabanshchikova and Polyanskii proved that the convex sets bounded by these ellipses have a common intersection point.
See Barabanshchikova and Polyanskii, Intersecting ellipses induced by a max-sum matching.
